- (config) `default_model` / `default_effort` in `config.json` set the default pair; a bad value takes that half of

body:
## 2026-11-23-model-and-effort-at-launch — Surface: cli: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Surface: cli
**Change:** ~ contract/cli-exit-codes/2 · promise: was «Clap usage text (never from `viola hook`), or the fixed `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` line (oversize `viola answer`) or `UNUSABLE_TEXT` line (unusable `viola send`) on stderr, whatever `--json` says; no document.»; now «Clap usage text (never from `viola hook`), or the fixed `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` line (oversize `viola answer`), `UNUSABLE_TEXT` line (unusable `viola send`) or `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES` line (a pair after `--` of `run` or `revive`) on stderr, whatever `--json` says; no document.»
**Why:** contract/cli-exit-codes/2: run and revive now refuse a pair after the dashes with the one fixed line PAIR_AFTER_DASHES at exit 2, so the row's named fixed lines are short of it.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T10-41-57Z-wrap/

- Arguments mirror channel params: `viola send <target>` (text from stdin or `--file`), `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]`, `viola last <target>`, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>` (response JSON from stdin/`--file`), `viola pause <target>`, `viola release <target>` (a `--budget` flag is a usage error, exit 2), `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>`; `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [-- <child args>]` and `viola revive <name> --list` send no channel frame (`--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork`, `--model`, `--effort` and the trailing arguments); `viola run --parent <NAME>` declares the instance's parent (one equal to its own name a usage error, exit 2, before anything is read; with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` is taken as parent only, dropped when it equals the own name) and `viola run --role <WORD>` its role, a code word; `viola run --model <MODEL>` names the model handed to the child, a model word, and `viola run --effort <EFFORT>` its effort, one of the five effort words, a value failing its shape a usage error, exit 2, and with none given each is the `config.json` default, else the compiled default.

- `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`; keys: `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`; the only source of the process-log level, `RUST_LOG` having no effect; obs D-15), `claude_env_keep` (the R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty; a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect; keeping `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` makes `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` read its value to locate the Claude config file), `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start; any other value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected` line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded), `verify_new_cli` (a JSON boolean, default false, turning on the `viola run` / `viola revive` start's automatic verify of a claude version with no attempted stamps entry; any other value reads false with one `parse-rejected` config-json `malformed` line), `default_model` (a string of the model word shape, default the model half of `DEFAULT_PAIR`) and `default_effort` (one of the five effort words, default the effort half of `DEFAULT_PAIR`), each bad value taking that half with one `parse-rejected` config-json `malformed` line, and no value disabling a control.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config; VH reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` human/harness; the wrapper sets `driver` only on the in-flight send's own prompt and relabels a CLI-fired scheduled wake `harness`). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the four flag literals `--resume`, `--fork-session`, `--model` and `--effort` (`MODEL_FLAG`, `EFFORT_FLAG`), and holds `DEFAULT_PAIR`, the one compiled default model and effort pair, with the five effort words of `claude --help`; no environment variable sets the pair. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- New event kinds and refusal details are added ONLY here, never with Claude-specific names; `detail` values are kebab-case strings from a closed set per reason (`unknown`'s a code word or null). `EventKind` holds the kinds of `EventKind::ALL` (`budget-gate` is no longer one), the dialog kinds `question` / `permission` / `plan` among them, `link` / `unlink` (`data` keys `driver`, `driven`), `dialog-expired` (`data` keys `dialog_id`, `dialog_kind`; `source: wrapper`, appended once when a held dialog's hold ends) `lineage` (`data` keys `parent`, `role`, each a string or `null`; `source: wrapper`, one line at every start, log-only) and, last, `launch` (`data` keys `model`, `effort`, both strings; `source: wrapper`, one line at every start after `lineage`, log-only); `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE` is the one wake set (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired`) the wrapper's `wait` and the channel's `outcome` both read.

- Readers: over-long lines (> `MAX_FRAME`) count as `torn_lines`; unknown kinds/fields are counted in `skipped`; a reader never writes (the next append heals a torn last line). A snapshot with an unsupported `v` or a parse failure → replay (`state-recovered`) through `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, whose five product callers are `viola revive`'s preflight, `viola list`'s `board::read`, `liveness::live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot unreachable, so the hook fails open) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone); the replay writes no file, rebuilds `lineage` from the log (the last `lineage` line replacing the held value) and `launch` (`{model, effort}`, the last `launch` line replacing the held value, a line with a non-string member reading none) and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines through the public rule `replay::apply_link_line` (a pair keeps its first `since` until an `unlink`; a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`), which the root bin's `LinkSet` applies as well.

- `run` start order (before the wrapper log opens, every start, `run`'s and a revived one, checks the home tree: `checked_exe` reads the exe's bytes once and takes their pin key, then `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree` checks the home, the instance's set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists — a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair, or the instance pair for an instance-level refusal, no log opened, no line and no child —, and the pin step pins those same bytes through `pin_bytes`; the home is canonicalised by `canonical_home` once the wrapper log has created it, before the collision check, the pin and the endpoint bind): program resolution (a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`; it writes nothing) → collision check → pinned copy (placed once when absent, with no clobber, through `place_private_new`, and never replaced; SHA-256 re-hash on reuse and of a copy a concurrent first start placed first; a mismatch → exit 1 `pinned-hash-mismatch`, the file left as found) + plugin folder rewrite → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: `--version` with no user args, killed at 5 s, logged as a `version-probe` start/exit pair; the stamps read; `cli_version` / `cli_verified` (the start's final verdict: the gate's, its stamps read again after an automatic verify where one ran) into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; nothing printed) → `socket_dir_ready` (`src/cmd/run.rs`: `check_endpoint_dir`, create the parent only when absent, check again; a refused or uncreatable directory → exit 1 `socket-dir-refused`, left as found, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, the `unable:` / `hint:` pair and one `process-exit`; a `Server::bind` failure does not read this code) → exclusive endpoint bind (taken → exit 1 `squatted-name`) → any automatic verify (with `config.json`'s `verify_new_cli` on, default off, and no attempted stamps entry for the claude version: `viola verify` run once as a child, the home passed to it only through `--home`, only while holding the owner-only `ledger/verify.lock`, try-locked after the stamps strict-modes check and never the stamps lock, a held lock meaning no verify and an unverified start; an entry already attempted, a red one included, never verified again automatically; the start gating on the final verdict) → on a verified verdict, the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder written into the child's Claude config (located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it) → first snapshot (with `endpoint`, `launch` `{model, effort}` (the pair the start hands: `--model` / `--effort`, else the `config.json` default, else the compiled `DEFAULT_PAIR`; a `launch` line appended once after `lineage`), and `lineage` `{parent?, role?}` from `--parent` / `--role`, with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` other than the own name taken as parent) + heartbeat → `wheel` event → child spawn (R8 strip, `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN`, pinned folder first on PATH, `--plugin-dir`, then `--model <M> --effort <E>` before the caller's arguments) → snapshot rewritten with `child_pid`. A live holder or a fresh replayed beat → exit 1 `already-live`, a `stale` holder → exit 1 `stale-heartbeat` (the `run.collision_check` span's `outcome` reads `already-live` for both); a `gone` one is taken over at once. The collision check takes its caller's one snapshot read (`replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`): over a replayed snapshot, which holds no `pid` or `started_at`, it decides from the heartbeat alone, a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old refusing `already-live` and an older one free; a failed read or no snapshot is free. The first snapshot records the spawn directory as `cwd` when it is valid UTF-8.

- `revive` (`src/cmd/revive.rs`) resumes a `gone` instance through the same `start`: first the strict-modes check (`trusted`: `check_instance` before the wrapper log opens; a refusal is the state-files pair and exit 1 with no log opened and no line), on the start arm then the home-tree check (`checked_exe`, then `refuse_tree`: the home, the instance's `check_instance` set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, and for the running binary's pin key `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola`, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists; a refusal prints the home-state pair, or the instance-state pair when the refused path is the instance's, opens no log, writes no line and starts no child, and under `--json` is the `strict-modes-failed` document), then a preflight of four readings in a fixed order, stopping at the first refusal (`session-live` is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips it, a failed read passes, its `agents-probe` pair in `run-<name>.ndjson`; `already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` → `no-session` → `session-live` → `cwd-missing`, each one `human::refuse` pair and one `process-exit{exit_code:1}` in `run-<name>.ndjson`), then program `claude` by name on its own `PATH`, child arguments `--plugin-dir <dir>`, then `--model <M> --effort <E>` (each half the `--model` / `--effort` override, else the recorded half while it still parses, else the start's default), `--resume <id>`, `--fork-session` with `--fork`, then the words after `--`, spawned in the snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the folder its start's trust record is keyed by. It logs as process `run`, replays no launch spec but the recorded model and effort, keeps the parent, the role and the model and effort pair its real snapshot records, and its first record is `wheel{driver, start}`. `--list` prints `<ts>  <cause>  <id>` per logged session; under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, once its strict-modes check passed, it writes `process-start` and `process-exit{subject:"self"}` (`exit_code` 0, or 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, and with no name opens none. Both arms take `--json` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): every refusal of its start, a refused strict-modes check and a preflight refusal among them, prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start being `internal-error`; `client::refused_document`) on stdout in place of its pair where it has one, stderr empty, the same exit 1 and the same log lines; `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; `Launch` carries `json: bool` (`run` false, `revive` `args.json`), and with it true `refused_with` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) prints the document in place of the human pair before `spawn_child`; a `pump_child` error prints no document, because the child has held the terminal.

- Normalised kinds live only in `viola-core`, never with Claude-specific names: `session-start`, `turn-ended` `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks, scheduled_wakes, cause?}` (`cause` present only on an API-error turn end, one word of the closed nine-word `TurnEndCause` set: `rate-limited`, `overloaded`, `auth-failed`, `billing`, `invalid-request`, `model-not-found`, `server-error`, `output-limit`, `api-error`; absent on a Stop end), `prompt-submitted`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `send-issued` `{cursor, from?}`, `send-confirmed` `{cursor, confirmed?}` (`confirmed:false` only for an unconfirmable send), `send-refused` `{refusal, detail, cursor?}` (the CL-1 send records, `source: wrapper`; `cursor` absent for a refusal before `send-issued`), `dialog-expired` `{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` (`source: wrapper`, appended once when a held dialog's hold ends; it carries no question, plan or tool text), `lineage` `{parent, role}` (each a string or `null`, `source: wrapper`), `launch` `{model, effort}` (both strings, `source: wrapper`, appended once at every start, after `lineage`).

- `wait` wakes only on `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired` (the one wrapper-appended kind that wakes it, appended through `WaitFeed::appending`); `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `lineage`, `launch`, a harness-origin `prompt-submitted` and the send records are log-only. The wake is by event kind alone: every `turn-ended` wakes whatever its `background_tasks` or `scheduled_wakes`, and telling a finished turn from a paused one is the driver's.

- An unsupported `v` or a parse failure → ignore the snapshot and replay the log; replay recovers only `links`, `agent_session_id`, `wheel`, `lineage`, `launch` (`dialog_pending` reads false; the last `lineage` line replaces the held value, as the last `launch` line does, a `launch` line with a non-string member reading none). The wrapper appends no budget-gate line and the snapshot holds no budget field. As landed the classified read and the replay are library code (`viola_state::snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`, `viola_state::replay`) with product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check has passed: `viola revive`'s preflight (one read for both its collision check and its recorded directory), `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::read` (a replayed snapshot gives a `live` row only for a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old, never `stale`), `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs, `viola link` / `viola unlink` and `viola mcp`'s frame tools; only a real snapshot gives an endpoint), `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot is unreachable, so the hook fails open) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone: `already-live` within `STALE_AFTER`, else free); no product code under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`. The replay writes no file but logs one `state-recovered` line (an absent snapshot is neither replayed nor logged), gives no `cwd` (a revive over a replayed snapshot is refused `cwd-missing`), and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines in its one pass through `replay::apply_link_line` (a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`). `replay::session_chain` reads the logged session ids in one pass and logs nothing.

- stdout = results (`viola mcp` writes only MCP frames, and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr when its home or `diagnostics/` fails `check_path`); stderr = the TTY-only context lines (`waiting:`, the send issue line, `last`'s header), a `run` / `revive` start's one automatic-verify line (one write, ASCII, no SGR, only the parsed version and a closed word; none under `--json`), `last`'s `no message` for `null`, refusals `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>` (the exit-1 refusals of `run` / `revive` / `verify`, a `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked (stdout empty, no summary), `list`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal, `plugin install`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal (the home pair, stdout empty; Failure reasons are the closed list in test-plan §3 (`build-failed`, `verify-failed`, `run-exited`, `readiness-timeout`). A `release` whose `from` is not a string or that carries any budget key (true, false, a string or null) is a plain `-32602` (data null) after the release-from-driver check, with no `release-from-driver` line, no wheel moved and no record; its `channel-response` carries `detail` `invalid-params` on both sides at WARN. The lineage line and the launch line written at every run and revive start are events-log product audit data: each wakes no wait and opens no span, writes no process-log line and no terminal byte of its own. The wrapper's stdin typed mark and its held scheduled-wakes count are in-memory state that open no span and write no line of their own, and carry no key and no prompt text. The cut mark a cut paste leaves is in-memory wrapper state too: it opens no span and writes no line of its own, its set showing as the cut send's `send-refused` `paste-cut` record and its clears as their own `prompt-submitted`, `session-start` and `session-end` records. The send's transcript echo read (the end offset before the paste and the tag count after it) opens no span and writes no line or span field of its own; its result shows only as the `send-confirmed` line inside `run.confirm_window`. A `send-refused` line carries `refusal`, `detail`, `side` and `wheel`, never `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` or `paused`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).
